cues.en: Today is my great pleasure to introduce Kevin Buzzard. He's a professor of pure mathematics at Imperial College. He received the Whitehead Award for his distinguished work in number theory in 2002. He also received the Senior Barric Award in 2008. He's a number theorist. He's also interested in formalizing mathematics, AI for math, and how technology can improve math education.
cues.zh: 今天我非常荣幸能向大家介绍 Kevin Buzzard。他是帝国理工学院的纯数学教授。他在2002年因在数论领域的杰出贡献荣获怀特海德奖。他还在2008年荣获了高级贝里克奖。他是一位数论学家。他也对数学形式化、AI 数学应用，以及如何通过技术改善数学教育很感兴趣。

cues.en: Kevin is extremely popular with his students. I met him and many of them last year had flocked. As a last remark, as many of you know, Daniel Selson is starting the International Mathematical Olympiads Grand Challenge, where the goal is to get a gold medal in this challenging and prestigious competition. A few weeks ago, Madden found out that Kevin is a master puzzle solver.
cues.zh: Kevin 非常受学生欢迎。我去年见过他和他的许多学生，大家蜂拥而至。最后提一句，很多人都知道，Daniel Selson 发起了国际数学奥林匹克大挑战，目标是在这项极具挑战性且声誉卓著的竞赛中摘得金牌。几周前，Madden 发现 Kevin 是一位解谜大师。

cues.en: He got a perfect score when he was a student, a gold medal. And today, Daniel and I had the pleasure to see him in action solving some of these puzzles. And it was human ingenuity at its best and how many magical steps are needed for solving them, the problems in this competition. The competition has six mathematical puzzles. Only the top students participate. And many of them can solve only or two of these problems. If you think Go is hard,
cues.zh: 他学生时代曾拿到过满分金牌。今天，Daniel 和我非常有幸亲眼目睹他现场解开其中的一些难题。这可以说是人类智慧的极致展现，在解决这项竞赛的题目时，需要踏出多少不可思议的神来之笔。比赛一共有六道数学谜题。只有最顶尖的学生才能参赛。而他们中的许多人也只能解出一两道题。如果你觉得围棋很难，

cues.en: is a finite action space. In this competition is an infinite action space and with many magical moves that demonstrate human ingenuity. Today, Kevin's going to talk about the future of mathematics and how technology is affecting it. Thank you. Thank you for the invitation. Thank you for the introduction. So as he says,
cues.zh: 围棋的动作空间还是有限的。而在这项竞赛中，动作空间是无限的，充斥着展示人类智慧的奇招妙招。今天，Kevin 将探讨数学的未来以及技术正如何对其产生影响。谢谢大家。感谢各位的邀请，也感谢刚才的介绍。正如他所说，

cues.en: Professor of Pure Mathematics at Imperial College London. I'm an algebraic number theorist. I have no background in computing at all. I've used computers completely informally. I've written Python code to solve games on my phone and things like this. But no programming background at all. I've used computer algebra packages. In particular, I've used Sage written by William Stein who's here with us to do calculations, to do computation. I want to check a million examples of something.
cues.zh: 我是伦敦帝国理工学院的纯数学教授。我是一名代数数论学者。我完全没有计算机背景。我对电脑的使用完全是业余水平。我写过 Python 代码来破解手机游戏之类的事情。但根本没有任何专业的编程背景。我用过计算机代数包。尤其是用过在座的 William Stein 编写的 Sage，来做一些计算。比如我想检验某件事的一百万个例子。

cues.en: But really, I'm interested in theorem proving, and there's theorem proving software nowadays, and I work in a regular math department, and no one in my math department has heard of this theorem proving software. It even has theorem in the title, some of its stuff. This is supposed to be for mathematicians, but no mathematicians use it. So, in some sense, the most surprising part of the slide is that a mathematician,
cues.zh: 但我真正感兴趣的是定理证明，如今已经有了定理证明软件，而我在一个普通的数学系工作，我们数学系里根本没人听说过这种定理证明软件。这软件的名字里甚至都带“定理”两个字。这本该是给数学家用的，却没有数学家在用它。所以从某种意义上说，这张幻灯片最令人惊讶的地方，在于竟然有一位数学家，

cues.en: actually started to engage with this software. Yeah, and all my colleagues thought I was mad. So I started goofing around with the Lean Theorem Prover, which is the software that Leo was written, that Microsoft Research was written. The reason I did it, I'll get to it, but the reason I did it was because not for my research.
cues.zh: 真的开始去接触这款软件了。没错，我所有的同事都觉得我疯了。于是我开始摆弄 Lean Theorem Prover，这是 Leo 和微软研究院编写的软件。我这么做的原因稍后会讲，但我之所以这么做，并不是为了我自己的研究。

cues.en: But because I was given an introduction to proof course to teach, I was told to teach the basic introduction to proof course, and I started thinking about what a proof was. These computer theorem provers have an extremely precise definition of what a proof is. So that's how I got interested because of an educational reasons. Then it slowly dawned on me what this software can do.
cues.zh: 但因为我要教一门证明入门课，我被安排去教基础的证明入门课，于是我开始思考什么是证明。这些计算机定理证明器对证明是什么有着极其精确的定义。所以我是出于教学原因才对它感兴趣的。后来我慢慢意识到，这个软件能做什么。

cues.en: Now, I'm absolutely convinced that this software has an integral part to play in the future of mathematics. So, many of my peers don't think this yet, but many of my peers don't. I think it's inevitable, that's the point. I think it's only a matter of time before mathematicians start waking up and smelling the coffee. So, there's many data improvers.
cues.zh: 现在，我完全相信，这个软件在数学的未来中会扮演不可或缺的角色。我很多同行还不这么认为，但很多同行就是不信。我认为这是不可避免的，关键就在这儿。我认为数学家开始醒悟、认清现实只是时间问题。所以，有很多数据改进者。

cues.en: I'm not saying this because I'm here. I might be here because I believe this. That might be more likely to be true. So I started using Lean two years ago, but six months ago, I thought I should probably try and look at all the software available. I looked at all the software available just with this one goal in mind of doing all of mathematics, somehow learning, attempting to do all of pure mathematics. I'm absolutely convinced.
cues.zh: 我这么说不是因为我站在这里。我站在这里，可能正是因为我相信这一点。后者更可能是真的。我两年前开始用 Lean，但六个月前，我觉得我应该去看看所有可用的软件。我看遍所有可用软件，只带着一个目标：做遍全部数学，设法学习、尝试做遍全部纯数学。我完全相信。

cues.en: If you want to do all of pure mathematics, then Microsoft is currently the winner, hands down. I mean, that might not be true forever. But I think the lean, this is some technical issue to do with what type theory it's using and how one can use it. But at the minute, I think you're sitting on the goldmine. But in 10 years time, things might be very different. So I'm not saying lean is going to solve all the problems, but tools such as lean.
cues.zh: 如果你想做遍全部纯数学，那么目前 Microsoft 是赢家，毫无悬念。我是说，这也许不会永远成立。但我认为 Lean，这涉及一些技术问题，和它使用哪种类型论、以及人们怎么用它有关。但眼下，我认为你正坐在金矿上。但十年后，情况可能大不相同。所以我不是说 Lean 会解决所有问题，而是像 Lean 这样的工具

cues.en: are going to change the way mathematics works and probably quite soon. Maybe in the near future, they're going to be helping us. As a mathematician, I'm doing my research, I have some technical question about very, very complicated objects. You can't Google for the answer to that question. Google is a useless.
cues.zh: 将会改变数学运作的方式，而且可能相当快。也许在不久的将来，它们就会帮助我们。作为一名数学家，我在做研究时，会对极其复杂的对象有一些技术问题。你没法用 Google 搜到那个问题的答案。Google 没用。

cues.en: I mean, what's that being as well? Probably, these things just don't cuss it. If I've got a technical question, has the following technical statement been proved? I know exactly how I'm going to answer that. I ask my friends. I ask my peers. If none of them know, I ask the elders. I ask the experts in my area. Ideally, it would be nice to do that automatically. This is one of the many things that I think that software might be able to do.
cues.zh: 我是说，那又算什么呢？大概这些东西就是不管用。如果我有一个技术问题：下面这个技术命题被证明了吗？我完全知道我会怎么回答。我问朋友。我问同行。如果他们都不知道，我就问前辈。我问我这个领域的专家。理想情况下，能自动完成这件事就好了。这是我认为软件可能做到的许多事情之一。

cues.en: once we've made the database. I think also they can change the way we teach. So every year now, I get put in front of 270 undergraduates who've all just come out of high school and none of them have got a clue, the vast majority haven't got a clue what a proof is, like a rigorous logical
cues.zh: 一旦我们建好数据库。我还认为它们能改变我们的教学方式。现在每年我都要面对 270 名本科生，他们刚出高中，全都没概念，绝大多数完全不知道什么是证明，比如严谨的逻辑

cues.en: mathematical proof. They see heuristic arguments. They had told that the derivative of sine is cosine, and the proof involves drawing a very thin triangle and heuristically arguing that if you have a very, very thin triangle, a triangle with an extremely small angle, then the two long sides are approximately the same length, which is intuitively obvious. But that's not the kind of thing you can type into the Lean Theorem proof. So, they come with a very-
cues.zh: 数学证明。他们看到的是启发式论证。他们被告知 sin 的导数是 cos，而证明要画一个非常窄的三角形，并启发式地论证：如果你有一个非常非常窄的三角形，一个角度极小的三角形，那么两条长边长度近似相等，这在直观上很显然。但这不是你能输入到 Lean 定理证明器里的东西。所以他们带着一种非常——

cues.en: with a very vague idea about what a proof is and what they can get away with, and all of a sudden, they find out at university that they can't get away with anywhere near as much as they used to be able to get away. It is true that the derivative of sine is cosine, but we feel that this needs a proof, and the proof that we're going to give them is very different to the proof. In fact, the proof I was told at school is circular, the proof that the derivative of sine is cosine because it involves
cues.zh: 带着一种非常模糊的观念，关于证明是什么、他们能蒙混到什么程度，然后突然在大学里发现，他们再也不能像以前那样蒙混那么多。sin 的导数是 cos 没错，但我们觉得这需要一个证明，而我们要给他们的证明，和那个证明很不一样。事实上，我在学校里被告知的那个证明是循环论证，证明 sin 的导数是 cos 的证明，因为它涉及

cues.en: You do the algebra and you end up reducing to the case of zero. You need to prove that the derivative of sine at zero is cosine. So you have to compute sine of x divided by x and then take the limit as x tends to zero. The proof of this involves somehow drawing the graph of sine and saying, well, it looks kind of intuitively obvious. Then you say, and actually later on we'll prove. After a while you forget about the question that derivative of sine is cosine. The question is, what's the limit as x tends to zero?
cues.zh: 你做代数运算，最后会化归到零的情形。你需要证明 sin 在零处的导数是 cos。所以你必须计算 sin x 除以 x，然后取 x 趋于零时的极限。这个的证明会涉及画出 sin 的图像，然后说，嗯，这看起来直观上很显然。然后你说，其实后面我们会证明。过一阵子，你就忘了 sin 的导数是 cos 这个问题。问题在于，x 趋于零时的极限是什么？

cues.en: of sine x divided by x. Then once people have forgotten that that was relevant, you sort of say, well, later on we'll prove that derivative of sine is cosine. So that means that this slope must be one because the cosine of zero is one. Some circular argument is slipped in. So we get told rubbish at school and then I have to pick up the pieces. I got interested in Lean because I thought it was, because kids like software, right? I started 20 years ago, kids didn't use software because-
cues.zh: 就是 sin x 除以 x 的极限。等大家把这茬儿给忘了，你再顺水推舟地说，行，咱们后面会证明正弦的导数是余弦。所以这就意味着斜率必须是 1，因为 cos 0 等于 1。这就偷偷塞进了一个循环论证。我们在学校里净学了些胡扯的玩意儿，然后我还得来收拾烂摊子。我对 Lean 产生兴趣是因为我觉得，孩子们都喜欢软件，对吧？我 20 年前刚入行时，孩子们根本不用软件，因为——

cues.en: there wasn't software and now there's loads of software and kids have computers in their pockets. I figured, great, let's show them what proof is using software because they'll like it. So, that's how I started doing it. I think that this is almost certainly going to happen and this might happen. I just don't know. This is your problem, not my problem. Can you actually start making these tools do?
cues.zh: 当时压根就没什么软件，而现在软件多如牛毛，孩子们兜里都揣着电脑。我就想，太棒了，咱们就用软件来给他们展示什么是证明吧，他们肯定会喜欢的。我就是这么开始干的。我认为这几乎必然会发生，而那件事也可能会发生。我只是说不准。这是你们的问题，不是我的问题。你们到底能不能开始让这些工具——

cues.en: generate new theorems or generate new proofs. I don't know, but then again, I've seen computers do things like beating humans at chess and beating humans at Go, and so maybe they can beat humans at math. So I just don't know what's possible.
cues.zh: 生成新的定理，或是生成新的证明？我不知道，但话说回来，我见过电脑在国际象棋上击败人类，在围棋上击败人类，所以也许它们也能在数学上击败人类。我只是不知道到底有什么可能。

cues.en: I want to be there when it happens, and I want to understand what's going on. So in April, I met this guy called Christian Zegedy at Google, and he thinks it's all going to, within 10 years he says. He has a PhD in combinatorics, so he's an expert in a certain kind of maths. I've got PhD in algebraic number theory, which is a completely different kind of maths, and I'm rather more skeptical. I think that when we talk about mathematics, we might be meaning different things.
cues.zh: 事情发生时我想在场，我想弄明白这到底是怎么回事。今年四月，我在 Google 见到了一个叫 Christian Szegedy 的人，他觉得这一切都会……他说在 10 年之内就会实现。他拥有组合数学的博士学位，是某一类数学领域的专家。而我是代数数论的博士，完全是另一类数学，所以我持怀疑态度得多。我觉得当我们谈论数学时，指的可能根本不是一回事。

cues.en: he seems very bullish and one of his papers has got 15,000 citations. So you've got to take him seriously. But he has a team that's up there using Isabel, not lean, using Isabel, and he's going to do stuff. I don't think Isabel is good enough to do all. I don't think Isabel is good enough to understand all the mathematics, but it might be good enough to understand all of what he thinks is mathematics. So that's the situation.
cues.zh: 他看起来非常乐观，而且他的一篇论文被引用了 15000 次。所以你必须认真对待他。但他的团队在用 Isabelle，不是 Lean，用的是 Isabelle，他打算干一番大事业。我不觉得 Isabelle 足以搞定全部。我不认为 Isabelle 足以理解所有的数学，但它也许足以理解他所认为的全部数学。情况就是这么个情况。

cues.en: expand on various things. So who am I? I'm an algebraic number theorist. So ultimately, we're interested in questions about the non-negative integers. It turns out there are questions like Fermat's Last Theorem, which are very, very simple to state and extremely difficult to prove. This took us 350 years between the statement and the proof. It's very, very innocuous looking statement, completely of no use to anyone.
cues.zh: 再多聊聊别的事情。我是谁呢？我是一个代数数论学者。归根结底，我们感兴趣的是关于非负整数的问题。事实证明，像费马大定理这样的问题，表述起来非常非常简单，证明起来却极其困难。从提出命题到完成证明，我们花了 350 年的时间。这是一个看起来非常非常人畜无害的命题，对任何人来说都毫无用处。

cues.en: It's a puzzle, but it's just a great example of something that turned out to be extremely difficult. I'm very lucky because while I was a PhD student, my advisor and his advisor proved it. So I was all of a sudden in the middle of everything. I've learned a whole bunch of techniques that turn out to be suddenly extremely fashionable because mathematics has fashion. I learned a whole bunch of techniques and all of a sudden they were extremely fashionable and hello. Hey, do you trust the proof? Oh, I've read the proof.
cues.zh: 它就是个谜题，但它恰恰是一个极难问题的绝佳范例。我非常幸运，因为在我读博期间，我的导师和他自己的导师证明了这个定理。于是我一下子就置身于一切的风暴中心。我学到了一整套技术，它们突然间变得极度热门，因为数学界也是有潮流的。我学了一大堆技术，然后忽然之间它们就大红大紫了，然后就有人问，“嘿，你相信这个证明吗？”噢，我读过那个证明。

cues.en: and it's good. It's fine. I was always worried, it's so complicated. Yeah. It takes someone like you to say, oh, it's right. Yeah, but there's lots of us. A circular argument is lifting. No, there's lots of it. I read the Wiles and Taylor work, so that part's fine, but there's 50 references. But that's where we can help, right? I mean.
cues.zh: 而且这很好。没问题。我以前总担心，这太复杂了。是啊。得像你这样的人才会说，哦，这是对的。是啊，但我们这样的人很多。循环论证很提气。不，有很多。我读过 Wiles 和 Taylor 的工作，所以那部分没问题，但后面有 50 篇参考文献。不过这正是我们能帮上忙的地方，对吧？我是说。

cues.en: So let me fast forward a little bit. How does the proof of Fermat's last theorem go? It breaks into two steps. Firstly, you prove that the semi-stable Taniyama-Shimura conjecture implies Fermat's last theorem. Secondly, you prove the semi-stable Taniyama-Shimura conjecture. That's the strategy. Now, the big problem with software as it stands is that even though it's existed for 30 years, this theorem proving software, nobody has got round to even stating the semi-stable.
cues.zh: 那我稍微快进一下。费马大定理的证明是怎么进行的？它分成两步。首先，证明半稳定的 Taniyama-Shimura 猜想蕴含费马大定理。其次，证明半稳定的 Taniyama-Shimura 猜想。这就是策略。现在，现有软件的大问题是，尽管这种定理证明软件已经存在 30 年，甚至还没人动手陈述半稳定的

cues.en: Taniyama-Shimura conjecture. So, we can't even write the first line of the proof currently, and these things have existed for 30 years. So, the proof of last theorem is structurally complex. It involves, even though it's a statement about non-negative integers, the objects that are involved in the proof are incredibly complicated. Like they take pages and pages and pages to define. So, we've had to invent complex structures in order to prove a simple looking
cues.zh: Taniyama-Shimura 猜想。所以，目前我们连证明的第一行都写不出来，而这些东西已经存在 30 年了。所以，费马大定理的证明在结构上很复杂。它涉及——尽管它是关于非负整数的陈述——证明中涉及的对象极其复杂。比如定义它们要花一页又一页。所以，为了证明一个看起来简单的

cues.en: statement about simple structures. That's a general phenomenon of mathematics. Number theory is just undecidable in general. So, certain simple questions about the natural numbers you can solve easily and then somehow, I think this is part of the nature of mathematics. There are some statements which are easy to state but hard to prove, and then there are some statements which are easy to state but impossible to prove.
cues.zh: 关于简单结构的陈述。这是数学的普遍现象。数论一般来说就是不可判定的。所以，某些关于自然数的简单问题你可以轻松解决，然后不知怎么，我认为这是数学本质的一部分。有些命题容易陈述但难以证明，还有些命题容易陈述但不可能证明。

cues.en: But the proof-of-fertile series is long, you pointed out, but that's nothing compared to what we're doing nowadays because people are collaborating. It's easy to pass LaTeX documents around. People just write 200-page proofs, sync them up on the archive, and they look very professional because they're all written in professionally typeset software. The moment they're on the archive, other people can start citing them, even though they've not been refereed.
cues.zh: 但费马大定理的证明很长，你指出过，不过跟我们如今在做的事情相比不算什么，因为人们在协作。传 LaTeX 文档很容易。人们就写 200 页的证明，同步到 arXiv 上，它们看起来非常专业，因为都是用专业排版软件写的。它们一上 arXiv，别人就能开始引用，哪怕还没经过同行评审。

cues.en: if you trust the authors. Why would I cite a paper on the archive that hasn't been referred? One of two reasons. If I trust the author, I'll cite it. If I'm desperate for the result, and this is the only reference I know, then I'll cite it. But who cares if anyone's checked it because the currency, our currency is theorems. We want new theorems. So I just started to get nervous.
cues.zh: 前提是你信任作者。我为什么会引用 arXiv 上一篇没经过同行评审的论文？有两个原因。如果我信任作者，我就引用。如果我很需要这个结果，而这是我知道的唯一参考文献，那我就引用。但有没有人检查过，谁在乎呢？因为硬通货——我们的硬通货是定理。我们想要新定理。所以我开始紧张了。

cues.en: and that was another reason. Nervousness about the reliability of the literature was one thing that started making me think about using theorem provers, and then being told to teach a course about proof made it actually happen. So very briefly, the background, people told me that Haskell was kind of, I knew some Python, but people told me that Haskell was cool because it was completely different. I tried it, but I didn't get it, and then I was given this course to teach, and so then I thought I should go back to Haskell because it was-
cues.zh: 这也是另一个原因。对文献可靠性的担忧，让我开始考虑使用定理证明器，而后来被安排教一门关于证明的课，让这件事真正落地了。简短说下背景，之前有人跟我说 Haskell 挺……我自己懂点 Python，但有人跟我说 Haskell 很酷，因为它完全不同。我试了试，但没搞懂，接着我接到了这门课的教学任务，于是我想我应该重新学 Haskell，因为它——

cues.en: It was more mathematical. I don't know. I tried again the second time I did very well. I read this learn you a Haskell for great good. It was the second time I managed to get through it. It's hilarious. Then somebody asked some question about, this is a fancy theorem in mathematics. The odd order theorem is a very long proof and it was formalized in a rival system, a system called Coq. The proof was formalized. It took years to do.
cues.zh: 因为它更偏数学。我也不太清楚。第二次尝试时我学得很好。我读了《Haskell趣学指南》。第二次我终于读完了，特别有意思。后来有人问了一个关于数学中一个高级定理的问题。奇数阶定理的证明非常冗长，它在一个竞争对手的系统——一个叫 Coq 的系统中被形式化了。证明被形式化了，这花了好几年的时间。

cues.en: I thought, this is kind of cool because that's a relatively respectable theorem, the odd order theorem. We've got John Thompson of Fields Medal. The proof is quite low level. The odd order theorem is a question about finite groups which are relatively simple mathematical objects. The proof is lots and lots and lots of arguments involving finite groups. So it's different to Fermat's last theorem. Fermat's last theorem is a question about numbers, but the proof involves lots and lots of complicated structures. This involves.
cues.zh: 我觉得这挺酷的，因为奇数阶定理是个相当重量级的定理。它曾让 John Thompson 获得了菲尔兹奖。它的证明非常底层。奇数阶定理是关于有限群的问题，而有限群是相对简单的数学对象。证明包含了大量大量涉及有限群的论证。所以它和费马大定理不同。费马大定理是关于数的问题，但证明却涉及大量复杂的结构。而这个定理涉及的是，

cues.en: lots of ingenious arguments about finite groups, and it's the theorem about finite groups. So I goofed around with this and I thought, yeah, this is nice. There's a tactic framework and I could prove simple. The kind of things I wanted to teach my undergraduates. Then Tom Hales gave a talk in Cambridge.
cues.zh: 大量关于有限群的巧妙论证，而且它本身就是一个关于有限群的定理。于是我随便折腾了一下，心想，挺不错的。它有一个策略框架，我可以证明一些简单的东西。也就是我想教给本科生的那些内容。随后 Tom Hales 在剑桥做了一场演讲。

cues.en: in 2017 which was live streamed by the Newton Institute. These are links by the way. If I distribute the PDF afterwards, you can click on these links. Tom Hales announced that he was going to make a gigantic mathematical database that had all of pure mathematics in. He didn't name any software by name, but at the end somebody asked him what software was he going to use. He said, my proposal is Lean, and I thought I've never even heard of Lean.
cues.zh: 那是 2017 年，由牛顿研究所进行了直播。顺便说一句，这些都是链接。如果我事后分发 PDF，你们可以点击这些链接。Tom Hales 宣布他打算建一个包含所有纯数学的庞大数学数据库。他当时没有点名任何软件，但最后有人问他打算用什么软件。他说：“我的提议是 Lean。”我想着我压根连 Lean 都没听过。

cues.en: but I trust Hales. So I thought let's forget COC, let's learn Lean. So by this stage, I'm convinced that one could try and formalize all of that. I've seen what COC can do and I've realized that all the mathematics I know is just based on logic and COC understands logic. So I think, yeah, why not? Let's formalize all the mathematics. It sounds like an interesting.
cues.zh: 但我信任 Hales。于是我想，算了吧别用 Coq 了，来学 Lean 吧。到了这个阶段，我确信人们可以尝试将所有这些数学形式化。我已经见识了 Coq 的能耐，并且意识到我所知道的所有数学不过都建立在逻辑之上，而 Coq 懂逻辑。所以我想，行啊，何乐而不为呢？让我们把所有的数学都形式化吧。这听起来挺有意思的。

cues.en: Sounds like an interesting project. So, because Hales chose Lean, I think, right, I'm going to choose Lean. I'll give it a try. So, Coq I tried and then I moved away from, but Lean I tried and never moved away from because it seemed to me to be the right tool. Now, I believe it's the only tool that's currently available. I mean, other tools will of course appear. So, I stuck with Lean and now all I want to do, I don't want to do mathematics on pen and paper anymore.
cues.zh: 听起来是个有意思的项目。所以，既然 Hales 选了 Lean，我想，对吧，那我也选 Lean。我试试看。Coq 我试过，后来就不用了；但 Lean 我一试就没再离开，因为在我看来它是对的工具。现在我相信它是目前唯一可用的工具。当然，其他工具肯定也会出现。所以我坚持用 Lean，现在我只想做一件事：我再也不想用纸笔做数学了。

cues.en: because I don't trust it and I don't trust other people that use it, which is everyone. I'm having a midlife crisis. I think that's what's really happening. But given the choice between using free and open source software and buying a Ferrari, this is somehow a cheaper option. So I'm going to stick to lean and now my job.
cues.zh: 因为我不信任纸笔，也不信任其他用纸笔的人——而所有人都在用。我正经历中年危机，我觉得事情确实就是这样。但在用自由开源软件和买法拉利之间做选择，这居然还更便宜。所以我会坚持用 Lean，现在我的工作……

cues.en: is because I'm one of three mathematicians in the UK that's heard of this. By mathematician, I don't mean these people doing category theory and type theory. People that say they're mathematicians, but are proper mathematicians regardless of deep suspicion. When I say mathematician, I mean a proper mathematician. Some of the topology or analysis. None of these category theory people. These people are dying in my country. They're retiring from math departments. They're not being replaced. They're finding their way to other.
cues.zh: 是因为我是英国听说过这个的三位数学家之一。我说的数学家，不是那些搞范畴论和类型论的人。那些人自称数学家，但我要的是正统数学家，哪怕这说法招人怀疑。当我说数学家，我指的是正统数学家，做拓扑或分析的那种，绝不是这些范畴论的人。这类人在我们国家正在消亡。他们从数学系退休，没人接替。他们正在转向其他领域。

cues.en: They're being hired by computer science departments, philosophy departments. But for 20 years, we had no foundational people at all at Imperial. And the foundational people that taught me in Cambridge, Peter Johnston, who wrote some book about topos theory. He wrote the Bible of topos theory. He's retired and he's not been replaced. We don't care about these silly, we don't understand logic. There's no point in logic. Somebody checked that logic worked for mathematics, and so now we can just get on with our mathematics.
cues.zh: 他们被计算机科学系、哲学系聘用。但在帝国理工，我们有 20 年完全没有做基础数学的人。而在剑桥教过我的那些做基础数学的人，比如 Peter Johnston，他写过一本关于拓扑斯理论的书。他写了拓扑斯理论的圣经。他退休了，也没人接替。我们不在乎这些无聊的东西；我们不懂逻辑，逻辑也没什么意义。反正有人验证过逻辑对数学是有效的，所以现在我们只管做自己的数学。

cues.en: That's how we proper mathematicians think about it. So, I'm one of two or three proper mathematicians in my country that knows about this software. Because I think it's going to turn the entire world upside down, I think it's my job to try and tell them about it. So, let's start with the undergraduates. I love teaching, both my parents were teachers. So, I thought I'll try and teach the undergraduates to use this software. That's the plan.
cues.zh: 我们这些正统数学家就是这么想的。所以，我是我们国家两三个了解这个软件的正统数学家之一。因为我觉得它会把整个世界彻底颠覆，所以我认为我的工作就是试着告诉他们这件事。那就从本科生开始吧。我热爱教学，我父母都是老师。所以我想，我要试着教本科生用这个软件。计划就是这样。

cues.en: So, I just kind of threw myself in. I started a blog. Yeah, I've never done anything like that before. I'm on Twitter and started an undergraduate club and basically said, come along and we'll figure out how to use the software together. Because I'm a very visible lecturer, all the students know me because I've been teaching this first year course for several years and it's a compulsory course.
cues.zh: 所以我就一头扎了进去。我开了个博客。是啊，我以前从没做过这种事。我上 Twitter，还办了个本科生社团，基本就是说：来吧，我们一起摸索怎么用这个软件。因为我是个很显眼的讲师，所有学生都认识我，因为我教这门一年级课程好几年了，而且这是必修课。

cues.en: If I tell a bunch of students to go and do something, a lot of them will do it. So as I come to my club, so like 70 people will show up this first week and then we realize that actually the software is really hard to use and we don't quite know what we're doing and it's a very high entry bar. So lots and lots of people came in week one and by the end of the semester, there was about six people coming.
cues.zh: 如果我叫一群学生去做某件事，很多人都会去。所以当我办起社团时，第一周就来了差不多70个人，然后我们意识到这软件其实非常难用，我们自己也没搞太懂，门槛特别高。所以第一周来了好多好多人，到学期末就只剩大概六个人了。

cues.en: Then by the beginning of the next semester, there was about two people coming. So the two people were Chris Hughes and Kenny Lau. What was quite funny was by February, they were both better than me because they're young. I'm 50 years old. I can still learn things, but it just takes me some time. I have to be told things three times while they sink in. I'm not used to undergraduates being better. I'm shit hot.
cues.zh: 到了下学期初，差不多就只剩两个人来了。这两个人就是 Chris Hughes 和 Kenny Lau。挺逗的是，到了二月份，他们俩就都比我厉害了，因为他们年轻。我50岁了，虽然还能学新东西，但就是得花点时间。别人得跟我讲三遍我才能领会。我可不习惯本科生比我还强，我以前牛得很。

cues.en: I'm an expert puzzle solver. I'm a professor of algebraic number theory. I spend all my time dealing with these undergraduates and they can never tell me anything I don't know. That's been true for 20 years. I dominate the undergraduates. They can ask me the hardest question they come up with and I can answer it because I find the material trivial. For the first time in my life, undergraduates are telling me things that I'm interested in. So I thought this is really interesting.
cues.zh: 我是个解题高手，我是代数数论的教授。我整天和这些本科生打交道，他们从来不可能讲出任何我不知道的东西。20年来一直如此。我在本科生面前是绝对碾压的。他们能问出他们能想到的最难的问题，而我都能回答，因为我觉得那些内容太小儿科了。这辈子第一次，居然有本科生在教给我感兴趣的东西。所以我觉得这太有意思了。

cues.en: from a pedagogical point of view is that I'm actually trying to use this software and I'm getting stuck and they're telling me the way I should be thinking about mathematics. So this was extraordinary. These two people somehow ended up, one of them is now a maintainer of Lean's Maths Library. So two years ago neither of them knew anything about type theory or computers or anything, they were at school.
cues.zh: 从教学法的角度来看，当时我真在尝试用这个软件，而且被卡住了，而他们却在教我该如何去思考数学。这简直不可思议。这两个人不知怎么搞的，其中一个现在成了 Lean 数学库的维护者。要知道两年前，他们俩对类型论、计算机等等一无所知，他们还在上学呢。

cues.en: and now they're writing professional software. They're writing PRs. They've written 30,000 lines of professional level, professional code. So, I think that's kind of weird. So, then my institution started noticing that I was doing something a bit strange. They have a pedagogy transformation grant. They have money for summer projects.
cues.zh: 而现在他们正在编写专业软件，在提 PR，已经写了三万行专业水准的代码。我觉得这太不可思议了。然后我们学校开始注意到我在搞些与众不同的名堂。他们有一笔教学改革基金，有做暑期项目的经费。

cues.en: I've got three kids. I've spent 20 years never doing any summer projects because I was having to babysit my partner's a surgeon. So she's very busy. So I would babysit because I'm an academic. I would just take the summer off and do the childcare. My kids are all teenagers now. So for the first time last summer, I thought I can actually go to work during the summer and just leave them at home and just hope they don't burn the place down. So because I'd spent 20 years doing no summer projects at all, I said I'll do 20.
cues.zh: 我有三个孩子。过去20年我从没做过任何暑期项目，因为我得在家里带娃——我伴侣是个外科医生，她非常忙。所以我就负责带娃，毕竟我是个搞学术的，放暑假就专心照顾孩子。现在我的孩子们都长成青少年了。所以去年夏天，我破天荒地觉得我其实可以在暑假去工作，把他们扔在家里，只要别把房子烧了就行。因为过去20年我一个暑期项目都没做过，所以我就说：我要一次做20个。

cues.en: but will you pay for them? And Imperial came up with money to pay for 20 summer projects, and all of a sudden, I had 20 undergraduates. And I said, all right, let's just digitize bits of the curriculum. Take any piece of math that you thought was interesting. Let's type it up into lean. We had a really good time. And then October 2018, the new first years come in. I'm teaching my course again. And I've got this group of 10 students that actually know what they're doing.
cues.zh: 但你会为它们出钱吗？帝国理工拿出了资金，资助20个暑期项目，突然间，我就有了20个本科生。我说，好吧，我们就把课程里的一些内容数字化。挑任何你觉得有意思的数学内容，把它录入 Lean 里。我们玩得很开心。然后到了2018年10月，新一届大一学生来了。我又在教我的课。而我已经有了一群10个真正知道自己在干什么的学生。

cues.en: So we've got 70 people in week one and then I got like 50 people in week two and the students are talking to each other which is perfect about mathematics. So the search took a lot longer to die down and now there's a core group of 10 by the time. When the exams come, then it's only the hardcore people come. So I've gone from two hardcore people to 10 hardcore people. In October, it's going to start again.
cues.zh: 所以第一周有70人，第二周大概剩50人，学生们在互相讨论数学，这再好不过了。所以这股热潮消退得慢多了，到这时已经形成了一个10人的核心小组。考试来临时，只有铁杆的人才会来。所以我从2个铁杆变成了10个铁杆。到了10月，又要重新开始了。

cues.en: and now I've got lots and lots of people that know what they're doing, including several people that know what they're doing better than me. So that's what's happening with the undergraduates at Imperial College London. What have they actually done? We arrived at a perfect time because Lena just got all the prerequisites available to start doing mathematics the way a mathematician does, pretty much, not quite. Things like a theory of finite sets that we think of as trivial. It was thousands of lines of type theory code.
cues.zh: 现在我已经有很多很多知道自己在干什么的人，其中还有几个人比我更懂。这就是伦敦帝国理工学院本科生这边的情况。他们实际做了什么？我们来得正是时候，因为 Lean 刚刚具备了所有先决条件，可以开始像数学家那样做数学了，差不多是这样，但还不完全。比如有限集合理论，我们觉得它很平凡，可它曾是成千上万行类型论代码。

cues.en: was there in the maths library already, and so I just told the students, why don't you just take some random undergraduate piece of maths and formalize it? Because this is all undergraduate level mathematics. None of it was that the complex numbers weren't even in Lean when I started. My first achievement in Lean was to define a complex number as a pair of real numbers, and then prove basic facts about the complex numbers. I'm just thinking, if I can do this, I can do anything.
cues.zh: 它已经在数学库里了，所以我就直接告诉学生，你们为什么不随便拿一个本科数学内容来形式化？因为这些都是本科水平的数学。这些都不算什么——我开始的时候，Lean 里连复数都没有。我在 Lean 里的第一个成就是把复数定义成一对实数，然后证明复数的基本性质。我当时就想，如果我能做这个，我什么都能做。

cues.en: because that's exactly how I think about mathematics. So I just said, take a random theorem, why don't you prove it? Some of these things are quite hard to prove. Some of these are substantial pieces of work, but they're all done in the undergraduate city with very little help from me really. They just got the hang of it and they talked to each other and they worked us out. This software has been around for decades, but as a teacher, I'm interested in, where's the undergraduate mathematics degree?
cues.zh: 因为这正是我思考数学的方式。所以我就说，随便拿一个定理，你们为什么不证明它？有些东西相当难证。有些是相当分量不小的工作，但它们全都是在本科阶段完成的，其实我给的帮助非常少。他们自己上了手，互相讨论，然后自己弄明白了。这个软件已经存在了几十年，但作为一名教师，我感兴趣的是：本科数学学位在哪里？

cues.en: That would be, for me, a very natural thing to formalize, and it's not there in any of the systems. People just do bits and bobs. They kind of choose an area and they do that. Why can't we have one coherent body where all of the mathematics in a normal undergraduate degree is there in one library or at least in one system?
cues.zh: 对我来说，那将是非常自然的形式化对象，但任何系统里都没有它。人们只是零敲碎打，选一个领域来做。为什么我们不能有一个连贯的整体，让一个普通本科数学学位的全部数学都在一个库里，或者至少在一个系统里？

cues.en: Thirty years this software has been around, no one's ever done that. The proof of the odd order theorem, they needed bits and bobs from an undergraduate curriculum. They needed the third year group theory course and the third year algebraic number theory course, half of the third year algebraic number theory. So they formalized those bits, but they're not trying to make a library, they were trying to prove a theorem. So they did bits and bobs. Where is weird? It's just a different way of doing things. Why don't we just digitize our curriculum? The students-
cues.zh: 这软件都存在三十年了，却从没人做过这种事。当年在证明奇阶定理时，他们需要本科课程里的零碎知识。他们需要大三的群论课和大三的代数数论课，半门大三代数数论的量。所以他们形式化了这些零碎部分，但他们并没打算建库，他们只是想证明一个定理。所以他们就东做一点、西做一点。这有什么奇怪的？这不过是另一种做法罢了。我们为什么不直接把整个课程体系数字化呢？学生们——

cues.en: I don't know what that will achieve. It will be fun. It might teach the students something. I don't know. It might create an object that's never been created before. I'm a blue sky researcher. That's great. I do normal poses. I say I want to prove some theorems in the area that we're all proving theorems in. I want to prove similar looking new theorems. I think this is much more exciting. I want to make a new object. I want to make an undergraduate degree.
cues.zh: 我不知道这能做成什么。这会很有趣。可能会让学生学到点东西。我也不清楚。它可能会创造出一个前所未有的东西。我是一个做前瞻性研究的人。这很好。我平时也做常规研究。我说我想在我们都在证明定理的领域里证明一些定理。我想证明一些看起来类似的全新定理。但我觉得眼下这件事令人兴奋得多。我想造个新东西。我想把整个本科课程造出来。

cues.en: So there you go. So here's some undergraduates. I'm a really cosmopolitan international university. Ellen is German. Sangwoo is Korean. Kenny is from Hong Kong. Guy is French. Amelia is British. Jean is from Taiwan. Rohan is Australian. Blair is Chinese. Abby is Indian. Callus is Swedish. All these people have written code that's now in Lee's maths library. All these people, and every single one, without exception, none of them knew a damn thing about type theory or...
cues.zh: 所以你看。这里有一些本科生。我身处一所非常包容开放的国际化大学。Ellen 是德国人。Sangwoo 是韩国人。Kenny 来自香港。Guy 是法国人。Amelia 是英国人。Jean 来自台湾。Rohan 是澳大利亚人。Blair 是中国人。Abby 是印度人。Callus 是瑞典人。所有这些人都写过代码，如今都收录在 Lean 的数学库里了。所有这些人，无一例外，他们当初对类型论或者……

cues.en: coding or anything, they're all mathematics students, and I've taught them all to write professional code. These people here, Shah and Anker, Claire and Ramon, they've done projects with me. This is Ramon's MSC project, who's formalizing the definition of a scheme, which is an MSC level mathematical object that was in no system. Thirty years we've had this, fundamental Vladimir Vojvodsky got off Bealsmel for proving a theory about schemes, and then he went off and invented univalent type theory.
cues.zh: 写代码之类的根本一窍不通，他们全是数学系的学生，而我把他们全教会了写专业级别的代码。这里的这几个人，Shah、Anker、Claire 还有 Ramon，他们跟我做过项目。这是 Ramon 的硕士课题，他形式化了“概型”的定义，这是一个硕士级别的数学对象，以前任何系统里都没有。这软件我们都用了三十年，最关键的是 Vladimir Voevodsky 靠证明一个关于概型的理论拿了菲尔兹奖，然后他转身去发明了单价类型论。

cues.en: Ten years later, had he formalized the definition of a scheme? No, he hadn't. What is going on? An MSc student formalized the definition of a scheme, and then I started looking around seeing how it was done in the other systems, and I found that it wasn't there in the other system. cues.zh: 但如果 Coq 能做到，Lean 也能做到。据我所知，凡是 Coq 能做到的，理论上 Lean 也一样能搞定。但为什么大家不感兴趣呢？一个原因是我们根本不在乎奇数阶定理，因为它在 50 年前就已经被证明了。那之后过了 10 年，他们又证明了有限单群分类定理，解决了有限群领域的重大未解之谜。随后所有人都离开了这个领域，这个方向也就彻底沉寂了。

cues.en: So, the area has been dead since the 1980s and then in 2012, all these computer scientists like, oh, we formally verified the odd order theorem. There's nobody left who's interested anymore. They've just gone. They've retired and gone. The area is dead. We care about fashionable mathematics and finite groups are no longer fashionable. In some sense, this was a very poor choice.
cues.zh: 所以，这个领域从 1980 年代起就已经凉了，结果到了 2012 年，这帮计算机科学家突然宣布说：哇，我们形式化验证了奇数阶定理。可当时已经根本没人感兴趣了。大家都走光了，退休的退休，转行的转行。这个领域已经死了。我们在乎的是当下时髦的数学，而有限群早就过气了。某种意义上说，选这个课题实在是不太聪明。

cues.en: But in another sense, it taught us a lot of things, but I'm interested in marketing. I'm interested in marketing your software to my people, and this is a poor choice. cues.zh: 但从另一个角度看，它也教会了我们很多东西，但我看重的是宣传推广。我关心的是怎么把你们的软件推销给我圈子里的人，而选这个定理显然不是个好主意。当然，另一个原因是我们往往也足够傲慢。我们自以为懂什么是证明——只要泰斗元老们点头说没问题，那就是证明。那些泰斗们觉得奇数阶定理的证明没问题吗？他们当然觉得没问题，当年都给 Thompson 颁发了菲尔兹奖。

cues.en: We don't know where the errors are, but history says that the number of errors we've made is extremely small because we're good. We're mathematicians, we're good at smelling problems. If some argument doesn't quite look right or looks incomplete, or your gut feeling is that what's known isn't going to be enough to prove that result, then you can smell it. If you smell a bad smell,
cues.zh: 我们不知道错误藏在哪，但历史表明，我们犯错的几率极低，因为我们水平够高。我们是数学家，特别擅长嗅出问题。如果某个论证看起来不太对劲、或者显得残缺不全，又或者你的直觉告诉你现有结论根本不足以证明那个结果，你就能嗅出端倪。一旦你闻到了不对劲的味道，

cues.en: then you've got this 200 page paper. You don't read it from the beginning, you start looking at the statements of the lemmas and you're like, I believe that, I believe that, I believe that. cues.en: I think there might be some problems, but I don't think it's all wrong. I think that the chances of something big that we believe turns out to be wrong. I think it's actually quite small. First, we spent 300 years fiddling around.

cues.en: That's what works best. First, they understand it, then they formalize it, and then they really understand it, and it stays forever. So this is just too much. cues.en: you invent a bunch of sufficiently complex tools, and then you let the tools to all the heavy lifting for you. So the proof of course takes thousands of pages, but no one's really read it. What's the point of this?
cues.zh: 我也完全可以在这里把这些东西搭建起来，但它会耗费巨额资金。这需要耗费一笔巨款，而且问题是我们并不在乎，因为泰斗们已经说它没问题了。泰斗们都认定证明是对的，那再去核对它又有什么意义呢？所以做这件事存在一个阻碍，那就是没有任何数学资助机构愿意为此掏钱，因为其运作机制是怎样的呢？我提交我的基金申请，然后他们再转给数学家评审。这事有什么意义呢？

cues.zh: 花大把的钱去做一件毫无意义的事，所以这么推销也是行不通的；我们不在乎，是因为学术泰斗们都说没问题；我们知道它没问题，是因为我们给 Wiles 颁了奖；而且很有意思的是，其实没有任何人真正搞懂了它；数学是高度模块化的，顺带提一句，没有任何数学家搞懂了费马大定理的完整证明；他们很多人都读过 Wiles 的论文或参考文献，但我从没读过朗兰兹-特纳尔定理的证明，因为那全是大量的调和分析。

cues.zh: 但我理解它的陈述，也能引用并应用这个陈述，但我不知道证明过程，因为我的分析学底子不够，我是个代数学家；所以证明是模块化的，圈子里我们信任的各路人马分别验证了其中的不同部分；于是现在我们认为没问题了，但情况还在恶化；就像我说的，如今人们验证证明的方式是，只要有位泰斗说“这部分内容即将发表，但我现在先挂到 arXiv 上”。

cues.en: It's difficult to disrupt that. I say, look at that. Is this really fine? Are we actually doing mathematics? And the answer is yes, of course we are. That's how it's always worked. It's fine. They will appear. But in 10 years time, those 100 pages will probably have been written by some poor PhD student or postdoc. It's a tedious technical result that everybody knows. cues.en: So it's sort of funny and I'm beginning, do you trust a PhD student? I don't know because I'm getting a bit paranoid. That's not the way to sell the software. cues.en: I'm giving the colloquium in Durham in two weeks time and in Exeter. I'm going length and breadth of the country. In the EU as well, I give a talk in Germany about it all. It's great. I'm just basically being an evangelist for your software. It doesn't tell us anything, right?
cues.zh: 两周后我会在 Durham 开报告会，接着去 Exeter。我正走遍全国。在欧盟也是，我还在德国专门就此做了一场演讲。这太棒了。我基本上就是在替你们的软件当布道者。但它没告诉我们任何新东西，对吧？

cues.en: against the first question. Does it tell us any new theorems? I'll tell you what it does. It enables us to state old theorems. We can state the theorems. Schonzer proved a theorem about perfectoid spaces and got a fields medal. Now we can state that theorem. You can't prove it. Can we prove a new theorem? If you can't state it, where do you begin? Now we can state it. That's where you have to start. That's why I'm doing it.
cues.zh: 回到第一个问题。它告诉我们任何新定理了吗？我来告诉你们它做了什么。它让我们能够表述过去的定理。我们能够表述这些定理了。Scholze 证明了一个关于完美空间的定理并拿了菲尔兹奖。现在我们能表述那个定理了。虽然你还证明不了。我们能证明新定理吗？如果你连表述都做不到，你从何下手？现在我们能表述它了。这就是你必须开始的地方。这就是我做这件事的原因。

cues.en: Because you have to start somewhere and it's ridiculous and computer scientists say you've made a definition. It's like I'm making a class. Lean enables you to reason about code and you can prove a hard theorem. You can prove that this code does a certain complicated thing. You can prove a hard theorem and that's a triumph. I'm just defining a class. Anyone can do that. Maybe I've made a mistake. Sure. But maybe the definition is not right. The definition has changed since it was made.
cues.zh: 因为你总得从某个地方开始，而且这很荒谬，计算机科学家会说“你只是写了个定义”。就好像我在定义一个类一样。Lean 能让你对代码进行推理，你可以证明一个高难度定理。你可以证明这段代码确实完成了某种复杂的事情。你能证明一个高难度定理，那是巨大的胜利。而我只是在定义一个类。谁都能做到。也许我犯了个错。确实可能。但也许定义本身就不太对。这个定义自提出以来就已经变过了。

cues.en: It was tinkered with. If it gets tinkered with again, that's fine. I'll just take it with my care. I don't care whether it's right or not. We have something. So let's skip this bit because I want to stop on time. Formalizing definitions is difficult. Sorry, hello.
cues.zh: 它被修修补补过。如果它又被修改了，那也没关系。我继续跟着改就是了。我不在乎它现在是不是完全对。至少我们迈出了一步。那这部分就跳过吧，我想准时结束。形式化定义是非常困难的。抱歉，请讲。

cues.en: Yeah. I trust software more than I trust mathematician. It's as simple as that because I found mistakes. This is what's really going on. I referee papers and once I had a really bad experience referring a paper, I spent two years arguing with the authors that their proof was incomplete and eventually I won. But I was the referee and this took a lot out of me. I had young children at the time and it basically destroyed my, the authors were experts.
cues.zh: 是的。比起数学家，我更信任软件。事情就是这么简单，因为我发现过错误。真实情况是这样的。我审过论文，有一次审稿经历非常糟糕，我花了两年时间和作者争论他们的证明不完整，最后我赢了。但当时我是审稿人，这让我心力交瘁。那时我孩子还小，这几乎毁了我的——那些作者可都是专家啊。

cues.en: and it destroyed my trust in humans. My trust in Leo software has not yet been destroyed by any means. I think there's orders of magnitude. It's an order of magnitude more reliable. I don't care that it's not 100 percent. Lean doesn't have any ego. So why do I want them to use it? Because I've got a plan, right?
cues.zh: 这彻底摧毁了我对人类的信任。而我对 Lean 软件的信任无论如何都还没有被打破。我认为两者差了几个数量级。它要可靠上整整一个数量级。我不在乎它是不是 100% 完美。Lean 可没有自尊心。那我为什么想让他们用它呢？因为我有一个计划，对吧？

cues.en: Before we can start proving new theorems, we need to be able to state old theorems, and that's what we can't do because we can't state the semi-stable tiny armature and mirror conjecture because we haven't even defined the definition. So, there's not millions, there's only hundreds and thousands, right? There's not that many. I've done one, it took me eight months. I'm better at it now though. It won't take me eight months to do the next one. I've just written an EU graph proposal where I propose to do 10 more.
cues.zh: 在开始证明新定理之前，我们得先能陈述旧定理，而这恰恰是我们做不到的，因为我们连半稳定微型电枢和镜像猜想都陈述不了，甚至都还没给它下定义。所以其实并没有几百万个，也就成百上千个，对吧？没那么多。我已经做完了一个，花了我八个月。不过我现在更熟练了。下一个不会再花八个月了。我刚写了一份欧盟资助申请，提议再做 10 个。

cues.en: But what you would love to do really is just feed in the book. Just take the book apart, feed in the PDF, let the computer read it, and then interpret the natural language, and then that's great. It's just that's a million miles away, I think. I'm not an expert in this, but my impression is that computers cannot read human-generated mathematics.
cues.zh: 但大家真正梦寐以求的，其实是直接把书喂给计算机。直接把书拆开，输入 PDF，让计算机去读，然后理解自然语言，那就太棒了。只是我觉得那还遥遥无期。我不是这方面的专家，但在我的印象里，计算机根本读不懂人类写的数学。

cues.en: I think you actually have to write it properly. So to get mathematicians to do that, you have to teach mathematicians to write in this programming language. It's no good teaching them to write in English, and that's what I'm doing. I can't really get the staff to do it yet, so that's why I'm getting the students to do it. There has to be a new culture. We have to start making students write in this. If they want, they should be able to write in this language because I've got a thousand definitions I want to do.
cues.zh: 我认为你其实必须规规矩矩地把它写出来。因此，要让数学家做到这一点，你就必须教他们用这种编程语言来写。教他们用英语写毫无用处，而我现在就在做这件事。我现在还指望不上教职工来做，所以才让学生来做。必须建立一种新文化。我们得开始让学生用这个来写。只要他们愿意，就应该能用这种语言来表达，因为我有上千个定义想要去实现。

cues.en: it's maths and computer science, grant agencies should love this because it's synergy. But let's find out, let's see if it actually, I mean, there's problems. So as I say, this stuff's been for 30 years, but if you ask a random mathematician in my department what they're working on, they'll state a theorem and it will be impossible to state that theorem in any of the-
cues.zh: 这是数学与计算机科学的结合，资助机构应该会很喜欢，毕竟这是跨学科协同。但我们不妨看看，看看是不是真的能……我是说，这其实存在问题。正如我所说，这套东西已经搞了 30 年了，但如果你在我们系随便找个数学家问他们在研究什么，他们随口说出的定理，都根本无法用任何一个——

cues.en: any of these theorem provers because it will be about objects that computer scientists don't understand. It's as simple as that because computer scientists are not research level mathematicians. We're learning about P-adic Banach spaces and we're proving lemmas about P-adic Banach spaces. There's no definition of a P-adic Banach space. So the software, it's been around for 30 years and it still can't understand the statements of what we're doing. That's how far we are.
cues.zh: 用任何现有的定理证明器来陈述，因为那些定理涉及的对象是计算机科学家根本理解不了的。原因就这么简单，因为计算机科学家并不是研究级数学家。我们正在研究 p 进巴拿赫空间，正在证明有关 p 进巴拿赫空间的引理。可软件里根本没有 p 进巴拿赫空间的定义。所以说这软件都问世 30 年了，却依然读不懂我们正在研究的命题表述。我们之间的差距就是这么大。

cues.en: It's just farcical. It's just farcical, 30 years. It's time we got together. It's time we got together. So we don't see the objects that we think are sexy. So I just written an EU grant proposal, two million euros to just give me a couple of post-docs who can just spend their time formalizing definitions and formalizing famous mathematical conjectures and famous mathematical theorems. This has gone to the EU and-
cues.zh: 这简直太荒谬了。整整 30 年了，太荒谬了。我们早该携手合作了。是时候联合起来了。所以软件里根本没有我们觉得很吸引人的研究对象。因此我刚写了一份欧盟资助申请，申请两百万欧元，哪怕只给我配几个博后，让他们全职去形式化各种定义，形式化那些著名的数学猜想和著名的数学定理就行。这提案已经提交给欧盟了，然而——

cues.en: On the 31st of October, the UK is going to crash out of the EU with no deal, and my grant application will instantly become invalid. Because if we came out with a deal, we would be some kind of member. If we come out with no deal, then my grant proposal has failed. But the idea is like Trump loves Johnson, and the idea is that we're going to be president of America now. So yeah, remember me on Halloween.
cues.zh: 10 月 31 号英国就要无协议脱欧了，我的资助申请立刻就会作废。因为如果是有协议脱欧，我们多少还能算某种成员。要是无协议脱欧，那我的申请就泡汤了。不过现在的局势就好像 Trump 喜欢 Johnson，而我们好像马上要成美国总统了似的。所以啊，万圣节那天记得替我默哀。

cues.en: Because apparently, America are our friends. So if you want to give me $2 million or even half a million dollars just to fund a postdoc, Microsoft funded postdoc who's just quietly going to come and work with me at Imperial and just change the world, that would be great. That would be great, right? Tom Hale says we should make a database.
cues.zh: 因为显而易见，美国是我们的朋友。所以要是你想给我两百万甚至五十万美元，资助一个博士后——一个由微软资助的博士后，安安静静地来帝国理工和我一起工作，顺便改变世界，那就太棒了。那绝对棒极了，对吧？Tom Hales 说我们应该建个数据库。

cues.en: and Tom Houser is a very smart mathematician, we should just make a database. That's where to start. Let's just make a database of mathematical objects, and then let's state the theorems that relate these objects to each other. I think that's the next thing you want to do. Lean is the right tool currently. Lean is the only viable tool currently to do this. Let's tell it what modern pure mathematics is. Let's not prove any more big theorems that are 50 years old.
cues.zh: Tom Hales 是一位非常聪明的数学家，我们真该建个数据库。这就是起点。我们来建一个包含各种数学对象的数据库，然后再陈述连接这些对象的定理。我觉得这就是接下来的方向。Lean 是目前最合适的工具。Lean 是目前唯一可行的工具来实现这件事。让我们告诉它什么是现代纯数学。别再去证明那些50年前的重大定理了。

cues.en: Let's just define some modern stuff. Now, who's going to do that? People like me that know the mathematics and people that I'm making, people that I'm training. I'm a professional trainer. I've graduated 15 PhD students and I've taught 15 undergraduates how to write Math Lib Ready Code. I can train these people and when we've done that, it'll happen somehow.
cues.zh: 我们只要去定义一些现代的内容就好。那么，谁来做这件事呢？像我这样懂数学的人，以及我正在培养、正在训练的人。我是个专业的导师。我已经带出了15名博士生，还教过15名本科生如何编写符合 mathlib 标准的代码。我能训练这些人，只要我们做到了，事情自然就会水到渠成。

cues.en: When we've done that, we can make a database of stuff and a database of links between that stuff. This implies this or everything, every X with property Y gives us something with properties. We can just state the things that the elders believe. I don't care about proving them, that's harder. We can just state it and then we've made a big database of our beliefs. We're writing down our belief system.
cues.zh: 只要我们做到了这一点，就能建立一个关于概念的数据库，以及连接这些概念的关系数据库。这个能推出那个，或者任何具有性质 Y 的 X 都会带给我们某种性质。我们可以直接写下前辈们确信的那些结论。我不在乎能不能证明它们，那太难了。我们只要写下来，就构建了一个基于我们信念的庞大数据库。我们正在把自己的认知体系记录下来。

cues.en: And that database doesn't exist anywhere. This is a completely new kind of database. And then what we can do, we can start attaching things to the labels saying this was proved by this person in this journal. And then suddenly we can start searching it, right? Because you guys can do that kind of stuff. And then, you know, we can start asking basic questions. I don't know what we can do. That seems trivial. And that will be great. That will make mathematicians in the third world.
cues.zh: 而这样的数据库在任何地方都未曾存在过。这是一种全新的数据库。接下来我们能做的，就是给这些标签添加附注，写明这是某某人在某某期刊上证明的。然后突然之间，我们就能搜索它了，对吧？因为你们精通这种技术。接着，我们就能提出一些基本问题。我都不知道我们还能做到什么，那看起来简直轻而易举。这一定会非常棒，它能造福第三世界的数学家们。

cues.en: I have access to the elders, some of them work in the same building as me, but people that don't have access to the elders, they can use the database. Maybe we can make tools. Undergraduates, if I can say, the undergraduates who all work in this software, they don't have to mark their work. Instant feedback, that's what they want. 270 students and me, I find it very, very difficult to give them feedback. This is one of the biggest criticisms of my university.
cues.zh: 我有机会接触那些前辈大师，他们有些人甚至和我在同一栋楼里工作，但那些接触不到大师的人，就可以使用这个数据库。也许我们还能开发些工具。本科生们，如果可以说的话，那些在这个软件里做题的本科生，他们的作业就不需要批改了。即时反馈，这才是他们想要的。270个学生对我一个人，我发现要给他们反馈真是太难了。这是我们大学面临的最大批评之一。

cues.en: not enough staff, too many students. We love the students because they're paying our salaries, too many students, and they want feedback. They do some lemmas, they write some PDF stuff, they write some stuff on paper, it goes into the machine. A week and a half later, it comes back with some PhD student who's attempted to market, not always accurately. They're paying 9,000 pounds a year for that, and this gives them instant feedback. I think that's-
cues.zh: 师资不够，学生又太多。我们喜欢学生，因为是他们给我们发工资，但学生太多了，而且他们需要反馈。他们证点引理，写点 PDF，在纸上写点东西，交上去。一周半后发回来，某个博士生试着批改了一下，还不一定准。他们每年为此交 9000 英镑，而这个工具能给他们即时反馈。我觉得这——

cues.en: That's worth something. Then, of course, world domination. Then, I can give up. That's it. Thank you. Can you say a little bit about the features of Lean that made it well-suited for this compared to the other systems you tried? So, I looked at four kinds of foundational theory. They're set theory, which is what all math positions, if they learn anything at all, they learn set theory. But the only software doing that, automation is very difficult with set theory.
cues.zh: 这很有价值。然后当然就是统治世界。之后我就可以退休了。就是这样，谢谢大家。您能稍微谈谈，相比您尝试过的其他系统，Lean 的哪些特性让它如此适合做这件事吗？其实，我研究过四种基础理论。有集合论，所有数学家即便只学过一点，学得也都是集合论。但它是唯一这么做的软件，集合论的自动化极其困难。

cues.en: and I need automation. So I gave them on the set theory ones. Their simple type theory, Isabelle, the other big player really, in my mind is, and Isabelle, simple type theory is too simple. It's really great for doing 100-year-old analysis, and it's really great for proving theorems about spheres and things. But you can, I mean, you can, it would be extremely painful.
cues.zh: 而我需要自动化，所以我就放弃了基于集合论的系统。还有简单类型论，Isabelle，在我看来是另一个真正的重量级选手，但在 Isabelle 中，简单类型论太简单了。它做 100 年前的经典分析非常棒，用来证明关于球体之类的定理也很棒。但是，我的意思是，如果要用它……会极其痛苦。

cues.en: to define a perfectoid space in Isabel because the fundamental object is a dependent type. There's a sheaf of rings on a topological space. So I've got a topological space and for every open subset I've got a ring and this is a dependent type. You do it in a simple type theory.
cues.zh: 在 Isabelle 里定义完备拟空间（perfectoid space）会非常痛苦，因为其基础对象就是一个依值类型（dependent type）。那是拓扑空间上的环层。比如我有一个拓扑空间，对每个开子集都有一个环，这就是一个依值类型。而在简单类型论里做这个。

cues.en: You need a proper function, you can't have a dependent type, you need a function. So you take the disjoint union of all your rings and now you've got an object which isn't really a sensible mathematical structure. Then you put ring structures on subtypes of it and now all of a sudden you can't use any of the type class machinery because it's not actually a ring, it's a disjoint, it's a big collection of rings. So you lose the type class system. So I don't want to do that.
cues.zh: 你需要一个真正的函数，你不能用依值类型，必须用函数。所以你得取所有环的不相交并集，这样你就得到了一个在数学结构上并不真正合理的数学对象。然后你在它的子类型上赋予环结构，紧接着突然之间，你就用不了任何类型类（type class）机制了，因为它实际上并不是一个环，而是不相交的、一大堆环的集合。这样你就丢掉了类型类系统。所以我不想这么做。

cues.en: I mean, it's fast, it's faster than lean because it's simple. It's good for some of mathematics, but I definitely want to do all of it. So then there's univalent type theory, and I'll buy that. I think in quite a univalent way, that looks sort of good. But they've been around, Voigt-Vodsky and his chums are around for 15 years, and you look at what they've done and they've done nothing. They've defined a ring and a module.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，它很快，因为简单所以比 Lean 还要快。它适合做一部分数学，但我绝对是想做全部的数学。然后还有单价类型论（univalent type theory），这个我认可。我的思维方式其实挺单价化的，那看起来还不错。但他们已经搞了很久了，Voevodsky 和他的同僚们搞了 15 年，你看看他们做成了什么，他们什么也没做出来。他们就定义了一个环和一个模。

cues.en: If it's taken them 15 years and they've done nothing, then I'm very skeptical. Fifteen years in COP, they were really doing stuff. But Lean's Maths Library, when I arrived in 2017, that software is only a couple of years old, really, and it's modern. When was Lean 3 released? 2016. So within one year, the amount of stuff in Lean's Maths Library just completely dominated what had been done in 15 years in Univalent. I don't know what's wrong.
cues.zh: 如果他们花了 15 年却一事无成，那我非常怀疑。在 Coq 的 15 年里，大家确实做了不少东西。但 Lean 的数学库，当我在 2017 年接触时，这套软件其实才出来几年，非常现代。Lean 3 是什么时候发布的？2016 年。所以在短短一年内，Lean 数学库里的内容量就彻底碾压了单价类型论 15 年的成果。我不知道问题出在哪。

cues.en: with univalent mathematics. Of course, I hope that it will work. There's something else just happened, what's it called, errands. Someone's made a new system. I would love to see univalence work because univalence is really useful. We have to work around the fact that we don't have univalence, but we can do it because the system is powerful enough to work around it. That was one of the mistakes I made in formalizing schemes, is that I just assumed that univalence was obvious because I'm a mathematician.
cues.zh: 用单价数学。我当然希望它能行得通。刚刚还发生了点别的事，叫什么来着，Arend。有人做出了一个新系统。我很想看到单价发挥作用，因为单价真的非常有用。由于没有单价，我们不得不绕过它，但我们能做到，因为这个系统足够强大，可以让我们绕过这个限制。这也是我在形式化概型时犯的错误之一：作为一名数学家，我理所当然地以为单价是显而易见的。

cues.en: I wanted to rewrite X was isomorphic to Y, and I'd proved a theory about X, and I wanted to deduce the theory about Y. Then I was told that life wasn't so easy, independent type theory, and that's why I started again. I'd written this formalization of a scheme with two undergraduates, and I realized that with Mateson. We had to work around, we had to do a lot of diagram chasing, and then I gave it to another undergraduate and said, this is the mistake we've made, do it in a bit more of a universal property kind of way.
